correctness.rationale: Exact combinatorial d_n recurrence follows by disjoint inclusion/exclusion of n and n-k+c with 2c<k. The k-bit admissible-word transfer graph is strongly connected and aperiodic, giving a simple Perron root and positive leading coefficient without characteristic-root assumptions. The known eventual a_n recurrence has primitive nonnegative companion matrix and positive leading coefficient. Strict root separation is P(lambda)=-(lambda-1)lambda^c<0. Fixed-L truncation proves d_(n-L)<=sum_{m<a_n}R(m)<=d_(n-1), yielding exact n-th-root exponential base. For fixed c, u=lambda-1 with ku~W(k); mean-value expansion of P near lambda yields rho-lambda~u^2/(1+ku), hence log ratio~W(k)/k^2. Verified 18 finite parameter tests using exact independent-set enumeration and automaton count; finite tests are not general proof.

originality.rationale: The 2022/2023 primary S-LID paper proves the greedy recurrence and the subset-count recurrence, but presents the average representation rate only conditionally upon spectral assumptions and explicitly leaves Question 5 open. The new claim proves strict entropy separation for the entire eventually recurrent [k]\{k-c} family by a primitive transfer matrix, proves exact exponential n-th-root growth for truncated representation counts, and computes the fixed-c sharp W(k)/k^2 scale. The 2016 Fibonacci quilt analog covers a different legal-index family. Targeted published-literature and accessible mathematical-record searches disclosed no equivalent statement; this is qualified, not a uniqueness proof.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently titled studies of the same S-LID roots may exist.
The theorem for small k,c requires independent verification of eventual a-recurrence; no blanket unconditional claim is made.
The two prior recurrence formulas are published and any novelty assessment concerns only their new uniform spectral consequence and k-asymptotic.

value.rationale: Provides an unconditional quantitative answer to the originating paper's Question 5 in a nontrivial infinite family of greedy integer-decomposition systems and extends to every pair satisfying the proved recurrence property. Unlike conditional informal discussion, it proves strict exponential ambiguity and its exact spectral growth rate; the W(k)/k^2 scale quantifies how the effect vanishes for increasingly dense forbidden-distance sets. The natural object and rate are independently motivated by the published question, not an arbitrary slice.
